chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Ali ibn Riyab, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

No one is followed after his death with reward except for three things: a charity he established during his lifetime, which continues after his death until the Day of Resurrection; a charity that is endowed and not inherited; or a path of guidance he established, which he practiced and others practiced after him; or a righteous child who seeks forgiveness for him.

key_terms.سُنَّةُ هُدًى: A path of guidance or established practice that others follow
key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ: Charity, specifically ongoing charity that yields continuous reward
key_terms.صَدَقَةٌ مُوقَفَةٌ: Endowed charity, distinct from inheritable property

ai.seo_question: What three things continue to reward a person after death in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* outlines the three enduring channels of reward (hasanat) that persist after death, emphasizing the continuity of good deeds through tangible legacy, intellectual/spiritual influence, and familial supplication. In Shia tradition, this highlights the importance of establishing lasting institutions (sadaqah jariyah), disseminating beneficial knowledge (sunnah), and nurturing righteous offspring who serve as intercessors through their du'a, reflecting the communal and intergenerational nature of spiritual merit.
